subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — ACME Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-health.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@acme-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — ACME Health

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes during peak booking windows (95th pct latency > 2s, occasional 5s+ spikes).
- Cost unpredictability on public endpoints; need consistent unit economics for forecasting.
- Data isolation requirements for PHI-enriched requests (must be in a dedicated environment).

Goals you outlined:
- Move critical inference workloads to reserved/dedicated capacity to eliminate noisy-neighbor latency and get predictable throughput.
- Maintain regional (US-east) deployment with strict VPC-level isolation and customer-managed KMS.
- Target SLA: 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints and p95 latency < 200ms for 512-token requests.

What Redwood proposed on the call:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) sized for steady-state 40 rps with headroom for 120 rps bursts via autoscale policies.
- Private VPC deployment option with optional on-prem connector for audit-only workflows.
- Model variants and quantization advice to hit the p95 latency target while limiting token cost.

Open questions / follow-ups we committed to:
1) We'll send a mutual action plan + initial sizing worksheet (attached: ACME_MutualActionPlan-v1.xlsx). Ben and Lauren will propose a recommended node config and cost estimate by EOD tomorrow.
2) You asked for an SLA draft and escalation matrix — attaching our dedicated_capacity_pricing.pdf which includes SLA bullets; Ben will follow up with a formal SLA template.
3) Tech deep-dive: propose Wed 7/15 10:00–11:00 PT for a systems deep dive (routing, KV cache, autoscale behavior). Please confirm.

If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update the plan. Appreciate the transparency on requirements — looks like a straightforward path to reserved capacity for your critical workflows.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: ACME_MutualActionPlan-v1.xlsx, dedicated_capacity_pricing.pdf

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brenner <tbrenner@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — ACME Health

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 40 rps steady-state is our conservative baseline; we typically see short spikes up to ~150 rps during flash sales, so the ability to absorb 3–4x for 5–10 minute windows is important.
- For compliance: all PHI inference requests must never leave our VPC and logs must be retained for 7 years. Can you confirm Redwood’s private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and long-term audit log retention?
- SLA: 99.9% looks reasonable; can you share concrete remediation/credit language?

We can do the Wed 7/15 10:00 PT deep-dive — Tom will join from infra. Please include a short agenda and any pre-read.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of ML Platforms | ACME Health
agomez@acme-health.com | (212) 555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-health.com>, Tom Brenner <tbrenner@acme-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — ACME Health

Alicia — quick responses inline.

- Burst capacity: we recommend a baseline reserved pool sized for your 40 rps with an autoscale policy that allocates burst nodes up to 4x sustained for short windows. For the flash-sale pattern (5–10 min spikes), we suggest a burst buffer configured with pre-warmed nodes to avoid cold-starts.

- KMS / logs: yes — private deployments support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS / HSM options) and we can configure audit log routing to your secure logging bucket with retention policies (7 years) as part of the deployment checklist. We’ll include the audit log config in the MAP.

- SLA language: we have a standard SLA doc; the high-level remedial is credits pro-rated by downtime with a cap. I’ll attach the SLA template in the follow-up and highlight the escalation path (on-call infra -> account director -> CTO).

Tech deep-dive agenda (Wed 7/15 10:00 PT):
1) Overview of dedicated runtime & isolation (10m) — Lauren
2) Autoscale/burst architecture and pre-warm strategy (15m) — Ben
3) Networking & KMS integration checklist (10m) — Marissa
4) Q&A + next steps / MAP review (25m)

Pre-reads: attached MAP + pricing PDF. Expect a proposed node config: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline, burst pool of 8x GPUs with warm standby — final numbers after we get your traffic histogram.

See you Wed — Ben

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Tom Brenner <tbrenner@acme-health.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme-health.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — ACME Health

Thanks all — Wed 10:00 PT works.

One small ask ahead of the deep-dive: can Ben include a short slide or two showing expected p95 latency versus token size for the proposed A100 config (512 / 1024 tokens) and an example of how quantization shifts that curve? That will help our infra team make an informed sizing decision.

I’ll review the MAP tonight and share any internal constraints. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Tom

Infrastructure Lead | ACME Health
